name: Northern Italy: Milan, Venice, Verona, Lake Como, Bologna

cities.base: Brera or the Porta Venezia side: a walk to the Duomo and the Galleria, and on the Metro for the Last Supper and the Porta Romana trattorias.
cities.name: Milan

cities.base: Cannaregio, on the Misericordia and Ormesini side, or Dorsoduro: off the Rialto and San Marco crush, with Marisa, Promessi Sposi or the Accademia on foot.
cities.name: Venice

cities.base: The centro storico between Piazza Bra and Piazza delle Erbe: the Arena, Juliet's courtyard and the Duomo all sit within a kilometre.
cities.name: Verona

cities.base: Varenna, which has the station on the Milan line and a 15-minute ferry to Bellagio; or split the two nights, one in each.
cities.name: Lake Como (Bellagio and Varenna)

cities.base: The centro between Piazza Maggiore and Via Zamboni or Santo Stefano, so the towers, the Archiginnasio and Anna Maria are on foot.
cities.name: Bologna

places.name: Dongio
places.note: Bib Gourmand 2026 Calabrian trattoria at about 35 euros a head; order the fresh pasta, spaghetti alla Cetara is 18. Weekdays 12:00 to 14:30 and 19:00 to 23:00, Saturday dinner from 19:00, shut Sunday. Book.

places.name: Da Giannino - L'Angolo d'Abruzzo
places.note: Abruzzo cooking in generous portions at about 28 euros a head, the cheapest good dinner in Milan. 12:00 to 14:30 and 19:30 to 23:30, shut Monday. Book, and book well ahead for Design Week in April.

places.name: Mater Bistrot
places.note: Starter, main and dessert come to about 52 euros with the 3.50 cover; tasting menus 75 or 85, oysters 7 each, wine 9 to 13 a glass. Dinner 19:00 to 00:30, weekend lunch 12:30 to 15:00, shut Monday. Books out in Design Week.

places.name: Osteria La Semivuota
places.note: An osteria at about 40 euros a head, Google 4.6 from 465 reviews. Weekdays 12:00 to 14:30 and 19:00 to 23:30; Saturday is dinner and Sunday is lunch, so it covers the Sunday that Dongio is shut.

places.name: Duomo di Milano
places.note: Begun in 1386 under Archbishop Antonio da Saluzzo, with room for 40,000. The cathedral is free with a queue; the roof terraces are the point, 22 euros by stairs or 26 by lift. Daily 08:00 to 19:00 per a June 2026 guide, so confirm. Go at opening.

places.name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
places.note: Giuseppe Mengoni's glass-roofed arcade, opened in 1877, off Piazza del Duomo. Free, with no gate; Camparino in Galleria is inside if you want a drink at the Duomo end.

places.name: Castello Sforzesco
places.note: Francesco Sforza rebuilt it from 1450 on a Visconti fortress. 5 euros covers the Pinacoteca, the Pieta Rondanini, the Egyptian and instrument museums and the armoury. Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 17:30, shut Monday; courtyards free daily; free first Sunday.

places.name: Santa Maria delle Grazie and The Last Supper
places.note: The Sforza church of 1463, whose refectory wall survived the raid of 15 August 1943 behind sandbags. Book ahead, it is mandatory: 15 minutes, 40 at a time, released every three months. Tuesday to Sunday 08:15 to 19:00, shut Monday; check the price.

places.name: Pinacoteca di Brera
places.note: Open since 1809: Raphael's Marriage of the Virgin, Mantegna's Lamentation, Caravaggio's Supper at Emmaus, Hayez's The Kiss. Tuesday to Sunday 08:30 to 19:15, last entry 18:00, shut Monday; free first Sunday with booking, otherwise check the price.

places.name: Museo del Novecento
places.note: About 400 20th-century works in the Arengario since 2010: Pellizza da Volpedo's Il Quarto Stato, Boccioni and Balla. The top-floor bar faces the Duomo. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Basilica di Sant'Ambrogio
places.note: Founded by St Ambrose in 379 to 386 and rebuilt Romanesque in the 12th century; find the 9th-century Monks' Tower and the pulpit on a 4th-century sarcophagus. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Teatro alla Scala
places.note: Opened on 3 August 1778, reopened in 1946 and again on 7 December 2004. Whether its museum is open was not verified, so hours vary, check, and check the price.
places.neighborhood: Piazza della Scala, by the Galleria

places.name: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
places.note: The Temple of Speed, opened 1922: 5.793 km, 11 turns, 118,865 capacity. The Italian Grand Prix runs here in early September, when Milan hotels climb; the 2026 date was not verified. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Trattoria alla Madonna
places.note: A seafood trattoria by the Rialto at 30 to 40 euros a head, with cover and service on top. 12:00 to 15:00 and 19:00 to 22:00, shut Wednesday. Google 3.9 from 2,860 reviews, so it is the busy one; book.

places.name: Trattoria da'a Marisa
places.note: A locals' trattoria on the station side, far from San Marco, about 35 euros; one reviewer had a 50 euro seafood set menu. Lunch 12:00 to 14:00 every day; dinner 19:30 to 22:00 on Tuesday and Thursday to Saturday. Book.

places.name: Osteria Ai Promessi Sposi
places.note: An osteria at about 35 euros a head, Google 4.5 from 1,739 reviews. Tuesday to Sunday 11:30 to 14:15 and 18:30 to 22:15, Monday from 18:30, so it is open on the days the others shut.

places.name: Trattoria Altanella
places.note: On Giudecca, so take the vaporetto across; about 50 euros a head, Google 4.4 from 431 reviews. Wednesday to Sunday 12:30 to 14:30 and 19:30 to 21:30, shut Monday and Tuesday.

places.name: Cantine del Vino gia Schiavi
places.note: Cicchetti and an ombra of wine at the counter: 2 to 4 euros a glass, 1 to 3 a cicchetto. Weekdays 08:30 to 14:00 and 16:00 to 20:30, Saturday 09:30 to 16:00, shut Sunday. Google 4.7 from 2,902.

places.name: Cantina Do Mori
places.note: A cicchetti bar by the Rialto market, Google 4.4 from 1,152. Weekdays 08:00 to 19:30, Saturday to 15:00, shut Sunday. Its own prices were not found; the usual Venice 2 to 4 euros an ombra is the guide.

places.name: Basilica di San Marco
places.note: The first church went up in 829; this one was built from 1063 and consecrated on 8 October 1094. The official page could not be reached, so hours vary, check, and check the price. Go first thing, before the square fills.

places.name: Palazzo Ducale
places.note: Gothic from about 1340, with the Porta della Carta of 1438 and Tintoretto's Paradiso in the 53m Great Council Chamber. 35 euros with the Correr, 30 bought 30 days ahead; timed slots. 09:00 to 19:00 to 31 October, to 18:00 from 1 November.

places.name: Rialto Bridge
places.note: Antonio da Ponte's stone bridge of 1588 to 1591 over the Grand Canal. Free, no gate; cross it early, since this and San Marco are where the crowds sit.

places.name: Gallerie dell'Accademia
places.note: Public since 1817: Titian's Presentation, Veronese's Feast in the House of Levi, Giorgione's Tempest and Carpaccio's St Ursula cycle. It reopened on 28 October 2026 after a closure; regular hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Peggy Guggenheim Collection
places.note: Peggy Guggenheim's collection in Palazzo Venier dei Leoni, open year-round since 1985. 17 euros. Daily 10:00 to 18:00, last entry 17:00, shut Tuesday and 25 December.

places.name: Santa Maria della Salute
places.note: Longhena's church, begun in 1631 to keep the city's vow from the plague of 1630, a short walk from the Peggy Guggenheim. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari
places.note: Consecrated on 27 May 1492, with Titian's Assumption on the high altar and his Pesaro Madonna in the nave. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Burano
places.note: The lace island: lace-making since the 16th century, revived by the lace school of 1872, and painted houses that need permission to repaint. No access fee is charged on Burano, so it is the day-trip for a fee day.

places.name: Trattoria Al Bersagliere
places.note: Bib Gourmand 2026, a lunch place. Order bigoli con l'anara at 13 euros and pastissada de caval at 18; with the 3 euro service that is 34. Tuesday to Saturday 12:00 to 14:00, shut Sunday and Monday. Book.

places.name: Osteria Mondo d'Oro
places.note: Perbellini's low-cost osteria, opened February 2022 and Bib Gourmand 2026. Set formulas ran 29 to 38 euros in 2022, so check today's. 12:30 to 14:30 and 19:30 to 22:30, Wednesday from 19:30, shut Tuesday. Book.

places.name: Trattoria Al Pompiere
places.note: Ravioli di faraona at 22 euros and baccala mantecato at 28, with salumi from 16 and tiramisu at 10. Monday to Saturday 12:30 to 14:00 and 19:30 to 22:30, shut Sunday. Google 4.6 from 1,953; book.

places.name: Osteria al Duca
places.note: A fixed two courses for 26 euros: bigoli with donkey ragu, then pastissada de caval. Monday to Saturday 12:00 to 14:30 and 18:30 to 22:30, shut Sunday. Google 4.5 from 3,411 reviews.

places.name: Arena di Verona
places.note: The Roman amphitheatre, finished about AD 30, seating 22,000 today, with an opera festival since 1913. Hours vary, check; resellers list 10 to 22 euros, so check the price. Hotels spike in September, the opera season.

places.name: Casa di Giulietta
places.note: Juliet's house. The courtyard is free; the house with the Teatro Nuovo is listed at about 14 dollars, not an official figure. Tuesday to Sunday 09:00 to 19:00, Monday from 14:00. Google 4.1 from 91,110 reviews, so come at opening.

places.name: Piazza delle Erbe
places.note: The Roman forum, with Cansignorio della Scala's fountain of 1368 and the Madonna Verona statue of about AD 380. A free, open square; the Torre dei Lamberti stands over it.

places.name: Torre dei Lamberti
places.note: The 84m tower begun in 1172 over Piazza delle Erbe. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Basilica di San Zeno Maggiore
places.note: Consecrated in 806 and rebuilt Romanesque about 1138; see the bronze doors of 73 panels and Mantegna's altarpiece. The bell tower went up 1045 to 1178. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Castelvecchio Museum
places.note: Cangrande II della Scala's castle of 1354 to 1376, made over as a museum by Carlo Scarpa in 1959 to 1973. Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 18:00, shut Monday. About 10 dollars, unconfirmed, so check the price. Google 4.6 from 20,197.

places.name: Ponte Pietra
places.note: A Roman bridge of 100 BC; four of its arches were blown up in 1945 and rebuilt in 1957. Free and open at all hours, so walk it at dusk.

places.name: Verona Cathedral (Duomo)
places.note: Consecrated on 13 September 1187. 4 euros, or 8 for the four-church ticket. Weekdays 10:00 to 17:30, Saturday 10:00 to 15:30, Sunday 13:30 to 17:30. Google 4.6 from 10,447.

places.name: Hosteria del Platano
places.note: Lunch, every day but Tuesday, 12:00 to 14:00. Book the perch risotto alla moda antica, then missoltini or lake fish; a primo and secondo come to about 50 euros, three courses 67 to 69.

places.name: Trattoria San Giacomo
places.note: A Bellagio trattoria at 20 to 30 euros a head, Google 4.2 from 1,084 reviews. 12:00 to 14:30 and 19:00 to 21:30, shut Tuesday; book in summer.

places.name: Bistrot Antichi Sapori
places.note: Large, affordable portions at 20 to 25 euros a head, with weekday lunch specials; Google 4.3 from 3,111. Straight through 11:30 to 21:00, shut Wednesday, no booking needed.

places.name: Villa del Balbianello
places.note: Built in 1787 for Cardinal Angelo Durini and run by FAI, which sells the tickets on ticket.fondoambiente.it. Hours vary, check, and check the price before you plan the boat.

places.name: Villa Carlotta
places.note: Begun in 1690 for the banker Giorgio II Clerici: museum rooms and gardens at Tremezzo. 10:00 to 18:00, last ticket 17:00; the 2026 season dates and price were not read, so check the price.

places.name: Villa Melzi Gardens
places.note: The garden of the villa Giocondo Albertolli built in 1808 to 1810 for Francesco Melzi d'Eril, on the lake at Bellagio. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Castello di Vezio
places.note: A castle of the late 11th or early 12th century at Vezio, by Varenna, open to the public since 1999. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Villa Monastero
places.note: A Cistercian convent from the late 12th century, shut by papal bull in 1567 and rebuilt 1897 to 1909 by Walter Kees; now a house museum, gardens open since 1940. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Basilica di San Giacomo
places.note: Bellagio's basilica, Google 4.6 from 1,140 reviews. A reviewer says it is free; hours vary, check.

places.name: Tempio Voltiano
places.note: Alessandro Volta's instruments in a temple opened on 15 July 1928, in Como town at the foot of the lake. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Ristorante Al Cambio
places.note: Bib Gourmand 2026, out past the walls. Tagliatelle alla bolognese 18 euros, seven-layer lasagna 22, tortellini in brodo 20, cotoletta 38; cover 5. Weekdays 12:30 to 14:30 and 19:30 to 22:30, Saturday dinner, shut Sunday.

places.name: Trattoria di Via Serra
places.note: Bib Gourmand 2026 in Bolognina, about 35 euros on a 2023 figure. Book by phone, 051 6312330; there is no online booking. Lunch 12:00 to 13:45 Tuesday to Saturday, dinner 19:00 to 21:30 Wednesday to Saturday.

places.name: Trattoria da Me
places.note: Michelin Selected 2026 at about 25 euros a head, a 2023 figure. Tuesday to Friday 12:30 to 14:30 and 19:30 to 22:00, weekends from 12:00, shut Monday. One of two here open on Sunday; book.

places.name: Anna Maria Trattoria
places.note: About 25 euros a head on a 2023 figure, Google 4.0 from 1,958 reviews. Tuesday to Sunday 12:30 to 15:00 and 19:30 to 23:00, shut Monday, so it is the Sunday dinner.

places.name: Vagh in Ufezzi
places.note: The cheapest here at 20 to 25 euros a head, a 2023 figure; Google 4.5 from 541 reviews. Tuesday to Saturday 12:30 to 14:00 and 19:30 to 22:30, shut Sunday and Monday.

places.name: Basilica di San Petronio
places.note: The basilica on Piazza Maggiore, Google 4.6 from 6,108 reviews. Daily 10:00 to 18:00; the ticket price was not listed, so check the price.

places.name: Archiginnasio and Teatro Anatomico
places.note: The Archiginnasio and its anatomy theatre, the Teatro Anatomico. Monday to Saturday 10:00 to 18:00, shut Sunday; the price was not listed, so check the price.

places.name: Due Torri
places.note: The two leaning towers: Asinelli, 97m, built 1109 to 1116, and Garisenda, 48m with a 3.2m lean. Hours vary, check, and check the price of any climb.

places.name: Santo Stefano
places.note: The seven churches: a 12th-century complex of four churches around the Cortile di Pilato. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Santuario della Madonna di San Luca
places.note: A 3.7km portico of 666 arches, built 1674 to 1793, leads to the sanctuary church of 1723. The portico walk is free; go in the morning. Church hours vary, check.
places.neighborhood: San Luca, southwest of the centre

places.name: Pinacoteca Nazionale di Bologna
places.note: Bologna's national picture gallery. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Ca' Rezzonico
places.note: Longhena began it for the Bon family in 1649 and Massari finished it for the Rezzonico, facade about 1750. Now the museum of 18th-century Venice: Tiepolo ceilings, Guardi, early Canaletto views, Longhi's genre scenes. Hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Museo Archeologico al Teatro Romano
places.note: Mosaics, sculpture and bronzes from Roman Verona in the old convent of San Girolamo, on the hill above the 1st-century BC Roman theatre. Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 18:00, last entry 17:30, shut Monday. About 10 dollars; go late in the afternoon.

places.name: Galleria d'Arte Moderna Achille Forti
places.note: Modern art in the Palazzo della Ragione on Piazza dei Signori. 6 euros, 4 reduced, 2 for ages 18 to 25. Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 18:00, shut Monday. Google 4.3 from 677; an hour is enough.
places.neighborhood: Palazzo della Ragione, Piazza dei Signori

places.name: Duomo di Como
places.note: Begun 1396, west front 1457 to 1498, Juvarra's dome 1770; Pliny the Elder and Younger flank the portal, Luini and Gaudenzio Ferrari inside. Weekdays 10:30 to 17:30, Saturday 10:45 to 16:30, short Sunday hours. The price list is an image, so check the price.

places.name: Villa Olmo
places.note: Simone Cantoni's neoclassical villa for Marquis Innocenzo Odescalchi, built 1797 to 1812 and city-owned since 1924. The lakeside park, about 800 tree varieties, is free, 07:00 to 23:00; the villa itself opens only for exhibitions, prices not found.
places.neighborhood: Borgovico, 2 km northwest of Como centre

places.name: Museo Civico Archeologico
places.note: The city archaeology museum, a step off Piazza Maggiore; Google 4.5 from 3,927. About 7 dollars. 10:00 to 19:00, shut Tuesday.

places.name: Museo della Storia di Bologna (Palazzo Pepoli)
places.note: The history of Bologna in a Pepoli palace on Via Castiglione; Google 4.4 from 923. About 11 dollars. Friday to Monday 10:00 to 19:00, Wednesday and Thursday to 14:00, shut Tuesday.

places.name: Basilica di San Domenico
places.note: St Dominic died in 1221; his basilica was consecrated in 1251. See the Arca di San Domenico, designed by Nicola Pisano in 1264, with young Michelangelo's Angel, St Proclus and St Petronius. Free. 07:30 to 13:00 and 15:30 to 19:30; Sunday 08:00 to 12:30 and 17:00 to 19:00.

places.name: MAMbo
places.note: Bologna's modern and contemporary art museum in the Manifattura delle Arti; Google 4.2 from 4,967. About 7 dollars. Wednesday and Friday 09:30 to 18:30, Thursday to 20:00, weekends 10:00 to 19:00, Tuesday 14:00 to 18:30, shut Monday.
places.neighborhood: Via Don Minzoni 14, north of the centre

sources: sights-v2 2026-10-28: every bed meets the sights standard

destination.name: Northern Italy: Milan, Venice, Verona, Lake Como, Bologna
destination.pitch: Five stops on one fast rail line, built for history and food: the Duomo and the Last Supper in Milan, the Doge's Palace, Verona's Arena, the Lake Como villas and Bologna's towers and tagliatelle. Give it ten to twelve nights.
destination.caveat: Venice charged day-trippers 5 to 10 euros on 60 days in spring and summer 2026; 2027 is unannounced. Last Supper slots go months ahead, Bellagio hotels average over 1,000 pounds a night in August, and Verona hotels spike in September for the opera. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Milan's Galleria and Brera, Venice from the Rialto to Cannaregio, Verona's Piazza delle Erbe and Ponte Pietra, and Bologna's Due Torri and the 3.7km San Luca portico.
because.food: Seven-layer lasagna at Al Cambio in Bologna, bigoli con l'anara at Al Bersagliere in Verona, perch risotto at Hosteria del Platano in Varenna, and cicchetti at Schiavi in Venice.
because.nature: Lake Como: the gardens of Villa Carlotta at Tremezzo and Villa Melzi in Bellagio, Villa del Balbianello, and the 15-minute ferry between Varenna and Bellagio.
because.culture: The Last Supper and Brera's Caravaggio in Milan, Tintoretto's Paradiso in the Doge's Palace and Titian at the Frari, Scarpa's Castelvecchio in Verona, the Archiginnasio in Bologna.
